Game Concept: The player controls an armed character who automatically moves forward and must aim and shoot giant monsters, zombies, and waves of enemies.

Simple controls: swipe your finger to aim.
Automatic shooting when enemies are in range.
Enemies become stronger and more numerous over time.
Fight giant Boss monsters at the end of each level.
Earn coins by defeating enemies.
Upgrade weapon damage, shooting speed, and firepower.
Unlock different weapons with unique shooting effects.
Each level introduces new enemies and challenges.
Graphics: Simple 2D graphics, colorful environments, satisfying explosions, smooth animations, and exciting shooting effects.
Performance: Very lightweight, optimized for low-end Android devices, with smooth gameplay and fast loading. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

Enemies become stronger and more numerous over time.

Upgrade weapon damage, shooting speed, and firepower.
Unlock different weapons with unique shooting effects.
Each level introduces new enemies and challenges.
Graphics: Simple 2D graphics, colorful environments, satisfying explosions, smooth animations, and exciting shooting effects.
Performance: Very lightweight, optimized for low-end Android devices, with smooth gameplay and fast loading. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

## Objective
- Build a complete, lightweight, playable 2D arcade shooter inspired by mobile game ads, supporting phones and tablets.
- Deliver swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating enemy waves, boss fights, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.

## Requirements
- Keep the game lightweight and performant on low-end Android devices.
- Use colorful 2D graphics, smooth animations, explosions, and satisfying shooting effects.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implement as a standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript game using a hand-drawn canvas, with no game engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Game title and theme chosen: **GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile**.
- Include synthesized audio, persistent local save data, four weapon types, escalating themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game interface and screen structure in `index.html`.
- Created responsive styling and HUD/modal/armory presentation in `styles.css`.
- Began `game.js`: themes, weapons, upgrades, enemies, level scaling, save data, synthesized audio, DOM/viewport setup, scene management, and cached/scrolled environment rendering.
- Added local font files for Bungee and Outfit.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`; it currently ends after `drawForegroundGrass()` and does not yet include gameplay loop, actors, combat, controls, screen actions, or initialization.
- Run the app and verify gameplay, responsive layouts, and controls; capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` with player/enemy/boss drawing and behavior, wave progression, aiming/auto-fire, projectiles, collisions, damage, loot, and effects.
2. Implement armory purchases, upgrades, persistence, screen button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, and animation loop/initialization.
3. Start the app, test desktop and mobile layouts plus a playable run, fix issues, and capture/inspect the latest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens, HUD, controls, and DOM IDs consumed by the JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layouts, and screen/modal/armory styles.
- `game.js`: Current partial game implementation; primary continuation point.
- `assets/fonts/`: Bundled Bungee and Outfit fonts.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` currently references `player` in `resize()` before its later declaration; this is safe because `resize()` is called after declarations/initialization, but ensure initialization ordering remains valid.
- `index.html` loads `game.js` directly at the end of `<body>`.

- Complete **GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile**, a lightweight, playable 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets, and test it on desktop and mobile.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics, smooth animations and effects, and performance suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Test desktop and mobile layouts and gameplay, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the responsive screen structure, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented game definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, HUD updates, and canvas rendering for the player, enemies, boss, projectiles, and effects.

### Active
- Finish `game.js` with audio, armory rendering and purchase logic, input and button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Align theme selection in `drawScenery()` with `buildBackdrop()`.
- Test desktop/mobile layouts and gameplay, resolve issues, and capture/inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` after `updateHUD()` with the remaining UI, audio, input, and main-loop logic.
2. Fix the mismatch between `buildBackdrop()` theme selection and `drawScenery()` menu-sector theme selection.
3. Run and test the app on desktop and mobile, resolve issues, and capture/inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Main implementation; core systems and rendering are present, but UI/audio handlers and initialization remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive layouts.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `resize()` accesses `player` but is called after declarations/initialization.
- `buildBackdrop()` uses `Math.floor((sector - 1) / 2) % THEMES.length`; `drawScenery()` currently uses a different menu-sector calculation, which can mismatch the backdrop.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish remaining game systems, test desktop and mobile layouts and gameplay, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, resolve issues, and capture/inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State

### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented game definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, HUD updates, and canvas rendering for the player, enemies, boss, projectiles, and effects.
- Inspected UI IDs, game logic, rendering, armory styles, and available browser tooling.

### Active
- Finish `game.js` with audio, armory rendering and purchase logic, input and button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Correct the theme-index mismatch between `buildBackdrop()` and `drawScenery()`.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, address issues, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the remaining UI, audio, input, and main-loop logic in `game.js`.
2. Fix menu theme selection in `drawScenery()` to match `buildBackdrop()`’s `Math.floor((sector - 1) / 2) % THEMES.length`.
3. Run desktop and mobile tests, resolve issues, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay and canvas rendering are present; UI/audio handlers and initialization remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive layouts.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `game.js` currently ends after `updateHUD()` at line 1085; existing code calls `sound(...)`, but sound implementation and animation/input initialization are absent.
- `buildBackdrop()` selects themes using `Math.floor((sector - 1) / 2) % THEMES.length`; `drawScenery()` currently uses `(meta.sector - 1) % THEMES.length` for the menu.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish remaining game systems, test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, resolve issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented game definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, HUD updates, and canvas rendering for the player, enemies, boss, projectiles, and effects.
- Inspected UI IDs, game logic, rendering, armory styles, and available browser tooling.

### Active
- Finish `game.js` with audio, armory rendering and purchase logic, input and button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Correct the theme-index mismatch in `drawScenery()`.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, resolve issues, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the remaining UI, audio, input, and main-loop logic in `game.js`.
2. Fix `drawScenery()` to use the same theme index as `buildBackdrop()`: `Math.floor((sector - 1) / 2) % THEMES.length`.
3. Run desktop and mobile tests, address issues, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay and canvas rendering are present; UI/audio handlers and initialization remain unfinished.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive layouts.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `game.js` currently ends after `updateHUD()`; existing code calls `sound(...)`, but sound implementation and animation/input initialization are absent.
- `drawScenery()` uses a different sector-to-theme mapping than `buildBackdrop()`.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish remaining game systems, test desktop and mobile layouts/gameplay, resolve issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Test desktop and mobile, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented game definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, HUD updates, and canvas rendering for the player, enemies, boss, projectiles, and effects.
- Inspected UI IDs, game logic, rendering, armory styles, and available browser tooling.

### Active
- Finish `game.js` with audio, armory rendering and purchase logic, input and button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Correct the theme-index mismatch in `drawScenery()`.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, address issues, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining `game.js` code and complete the missing UI, audio, input, and main-loop logic.
2. Update `drawScenery()` to use the theme mapping used by `buildBackdrop()`: `Math.floor((sector - 1) / 2) % THEMES.length`.
3. Run desktop and mobile tests, address issues, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay and canvas rendering; implementation currently ends after `updateHUD()`.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive layouts.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- `game.js` currently ends after `updateHUD()`; existing code calls `sound(...)`, but sound implementation and animation/input initialization are absent.
- `drawScenery()` uses a different sector-to-theme mapping than `buildBackdrop()`.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the unfinished implementation was added; it does not confirm gameplay readiness.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish remaining game systems, test desktop and mobile layouts/gameplay, resolve issues, and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Test desktop and mobile, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented game definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, HUD updates, and canvas rendering for the player, enemies, boss, projectiles, and effects.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` passes.

### Active
- Complete `game.js` after `updateHUD()` with audio, armory rendering and purchase logic, input and button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Correct the theme-index mismatch in `drawScenery()`; it uses `(meta.sector - 1) % THEMES.length`, but `buildBackdrop()` uses `Math.floor((meta.sector - 1) / 2) % THEMES.length`.
- Test on desktop and mobile, address issues, then capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the remaining audio, armory, UI/input handling, game-loop, and initialization logic in `game.js`.
2. Fix the `drawScenery()` theme index to match `buildBackdrop()`.
3. Run desktop and mobile tests; fix issues, capture a current JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay and canvas rendering; currently ends after `updateHUD()`.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive layouts.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Existing gameplay code calls `sound(...)`, but audio implementation, animation/input initialization, and other remaining completion logic are absent.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.

- (none)

- Project files were previously reported as untracked.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish remaining game systems, test desktop and mobile layouts/gameplay, and capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Test on desktop and mobile, then capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented core game definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, HUD updates, and canvas rendering.
- Confirmed DOM IDs referenced by `game.js` exist in `index.html`.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`, which currently ends after `updateHUD()`: audio, armory rendering and purchase logic, input and button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Correct `drawScenery()` theme selection: it uses `(meta.sector - 1) % THEMES.length`, unlike `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()`, which group sectors in pairs.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, fix issues, capture a current JPEG screenshot, and inspect it.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the missing systems and initialization in `game.js`, and correct scenery theme selection.
2. Run syntax checks and test gameplay and responsive layouts on desktop and mobile.
3. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay and canvas rendering; currently ends after `updateHUD()`.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive layouts.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Existing gameplay code calls `sound(...)`, but audio implementation, animation/input initialization, and remaining UI flows are absent.
- `startRun()`, wave progression, combat, and run-ending flows are present; `finishRun()` handles coin banking and result screens.
- Project files are untracked; no gameplay, responsive-layout, or screenshot test has been performed.

12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish missing gameplay systems, test desktop and mobile layouts/gameplay, and capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.

- Test on desktop and mobile, then capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.

- Correct `drawScenery()` theme selection: it uses `meta.sector - 1` instead of the paired-sector grouping used by `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()`.
- Test gameplay and responsive layouts on desktop and mobile; capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the missing systems and initialization in `game.js`, and correct scenery theme selection.
2. Run syntax checks and test gameplay and responsive layouts on desktop and mobile.
3. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay and canvas rendering; missing input, armory, audio, scene flows, and initialization.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive layouts.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Existing gameplay code calls `sound(...)`, but audio implementation, animation/input initialization, and remaining UI flows are absent.
- `startRun()`, wave progression, combat, and run-ending flows are present; `finishRun()` handles coin banking and result screens.
- `drawScenery()` should use the same theme grouping as `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()`.

2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18:

20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish gameplay, test desktop and mobile layouts and gameplay, and capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Test on desktop and mobile, then capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented core game definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, HUD updates, and canvas rendering.

### Active
- Complete `game.js`: audio, armory rendering and purchase logic, input and button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Align gameplay state classes with `styles.css`; `drawScenery()` still uses `meta.sector - 1` instead of paired-sector theme grouping.
- Test gameplay and responsive layouts on desktop and mobile; capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining `game.js` implementation and relevant styles, then implement missing systems and fix theme selection and state classes.
2. Run syntax checks and test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts.
3. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot, then address any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay and canvas rendering; currently ends after `updateHUD()` and lacks UI/input handlers, audio, animation, and initialization.
- `index.html`: Game screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layouts, and expected state classes.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked. No gameplay or screenshot test has been performed.
- `spawnBoss()` and `updateHUD()` use `.active` for boss/combo, but styles expect `.show`; aim-hint logic uses `.visible` while styles hide via `.hide`.
- `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()` group sectors in pairs; `drawScenery()` currently selects themes using `meta.sector - 1`.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish gameplay, test desktop and mobile layouts and gameplay, and capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.
- Test on desktop and mobile, then capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented core game definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, HUD updates, and canvas rendering.

### Active
- Complete `game.js`: audio, armory rendering and purchase logic, input and button handlers, pause/retry/clear/death flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Align gameplay state classes with `styles.css`; `spawnBoss()` and `updateHUD()` use `.active` where styles expect `.show`, and aim hint toggles `.visible` where styles expect `.hide`.
- Fix `drawScenery()` theme selection to match the paired-sector grouping used by `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()`.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts; capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining `game.js` implementation and relevant styles, then implement the missing systems and correct theme/state-class mismatches.
2. Run syntax checks and test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts.
3. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot, then address any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay and canvas rendering; currently ends after `updateHUD()` without UI/input handlers, audio, animation, or initialization.
- `index.html`: Screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layouts, and expected state classes.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked. No gameplay or screenshot test has been performed.

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Verify desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, then capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented gameplay definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, canvas rendering, and some UI/state functions.
- Inspected `game.js`, `index.html`, and relevant CSS; confirmed the final function in `game.js` is `updateHUD()` and wiring remains absent.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`: UI/state handlers, audio, input, armory flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Correct HUD state classes and unify scenery/backdrop theme grouping.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts; capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Complete `game.js` event handlers, audio, armory flows, animation loop, and initialization.
2. Fix HUD class mismatches: CSS uses `.show` for boss/combo and `.hide` for aim hint; JavaScript currently toggles `active`/`visible`.
3. Align `drawScenery()` theme selection with `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()` sector grouping.
4. Run syntax checks and test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts.
5. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot, then address any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay simulation and rendering; final UI/state wiring is missing.
- `index.html`: Screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layouts, and expected HUD state classes.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- No gameplay or screenshot test has been performed.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish wiring the game, verify desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts, and capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim controls, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented gameplay definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, canvas rendering, and some UI/state functions.
- Reviewed `game.js`, `index.html`, and CSS; confirmed gameplay/UI wiring remains unfinished.

### Active
- Complete `game.js` UI/state handlers, audio, input, armory flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Correct HUD state classes and unify scenery/backdrop theme grouping.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts; capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish event handlers, audio, armory flows, animation loop, and initialization in `game.js`.
2. Fix HUD class mismatches: CSS uses `.show` for boss/combo and `.hide` for aim hint; JavaScript currently toggles `active`/`visible`.
3. Align `drawScenery()` theme selection with `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()` sector grouping.
4. Run syntax checks and test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts.
5. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot, then address any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay simulation and rendering; final UI/state wiring is missing.
- `index.html`: Screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layouts, and expected HUD state classes.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- No gameplay or screenshot test has been performed.

16: `mesa-vulkan-drivers`, `vulkan-tools`, and `xvfb` on Ubuntu. Serve

116: ```
117: 
118: Create a branch from the exact commit and make it the GitHub default branch:
119: 
120: ```sh
121: git push "https://github.com/$repo.git" "${commit}:refs/heads/$branch"
122: gh repo edit "$repo" --default-branch "$branch"
123: gh repo view "$repo" --json defaultBranchRef
124: ```
125: 
126: Keep the existing `main` branch and older test branches. Use a new branch name
127: for each commit so the tested revision remains clear and recoverable. The
128: workflow checks out the GitHub default branch when the issue title has no
129: branch metadata.
130: 
131: Create an SSH test issue with the required labels:
132: 
133: ```sh
134: gh issue create --repo "$repo" \
135:   --title "Check SSH connectivity on $branch" \
136:   --body $'# Check SSH connectivity on <branch>\n\nVerify the temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, authentication, tunnel, and remote response. Record concrete evidence without exposing secrets.' \
137:   --label Goal --label ssh --label OpenCode
138: ```
139: 
140: Create the issue after listener installation to trigger one native `issues` run. The
141: `Goal` label selects goal mode. The `ssh` label requests an SSH-only check in
142: the reusable workflow. Verify the issue labels and the selected checkout:
143: 
144: ```sh
145: gh issue view <issue-number> --repo "$repo" --json labels
146: gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow opencode.yml --limit 5 \
147:   --json databaseId,displayTitle,event,status,url,headBranch
148: ```
149: 
150: Confirm `event` is `issues` and `headBranch` is the default branch.
151: Check preparation outputs for the selected `target_ref` and `target_sha`.
152: 
153: Discover and follow the temporary SSH connection with the repository helper:
154: 
155: ```sh
156: bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo "$repo"
157: ```
158: 
159: Run the helper while the Actions job is active. It reports no command after the
160: worker closes the tunnel. If it reports no command at the start, inspect the
161: run steps and logs before changing the SSH secret. `AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED:
162: true` proves that GitHub received the public-key secret; it does not prove that
163: the tunnel or SSH service started.
164: 
165: After testing, restore the normal default branch if required:
166: 
167: ```sh
168: gh repo edit "$repo" --default-branch main
169: ```
170: 
171: Project acceptance testing is live production testing. Manually create a real
172: GitHub issue with the required labels and prompt, then verify the resulting
173: issue run, exactly one execution runner/session, and the completed production
174: outcome. Do not use unit tests as the testing strategy; local checks such as
175: `actionlint` and `git diff --check` are only static safeguards before the live
176: test.
177: 
178: For an issue-triggered run with `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` configured, verify
179: these checkpoints in order:
180: 
181: 1. `Start AgentsWeb SSH session` succeeds.
182: 2. `Post temporary SSH connection command` succeeds.
183: 3. `Verify AgentsWeb SSH availability` succeeds.
184: 4. `Run OpenCode` succeeds.
185: 5. `Mark SSH session closed` and `Clean up AgentsWeb SSH session` succeed.
186: 6. The expected branch and immutable commit exist.
187: 
188: The verification loop must confirm a browser entrypoint before public-app and
189: Pages checks: either `$PROJECT_DIR/index.html` or `$PROJECT_DIR/dist/index.html`
190: must exist, and remediation retries must repeat that check. Static root
191: `index.html` apps are copied to a temporary Pages directory; built
192: `dist/index.html` apps are published directly.
193: 
194: When `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY` is missing, the SSH session and SSH-based
195: verification steps must be skipped. OpenCode Web, the Cloudflare session URL,
196: and the browser-based workflow path must still run; the access comment should
197: omit SSH instructions and cleanup must not report an SSH session closure.
198: 
199: The AgentsWeb public port must be derived from `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, not
200: `GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER`. Run numbers restart at `1` for each repository, which made
201: the first OMG run in every newly installed repository contend for port `32001`
202: and close during SSH verification. The globally unique run ID spreads those
203: runs across the broker's `32000-32999` port range.
204: 
205: Validate workflow edits locally with:
206: 
207: ```sh
208: actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml .github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml .github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml
209: git diff --check
210: ```
211: 
212: Create an issue with `OpenCode` and `test` for a synthetic-generation run. Copy the committed fixture and import a completed conversation into the real OpenCode server. Exercise the production checkpoint, startup, capture, and deployment path. Require a ready deployment with desktop/mobile screenshots. Keep logs in the run release and skip the five-hour hold for synthetic runs.
213: 
214: The caller must grant every permission requested by the reusable workflow.
215: Otherwise GitHub rejects the run at startup before creating a job, even when
216: `actionlint` succeeds.
217: 
218: For goal support, create an issue with both `Goal` and `OpenCode`. Verify one
219: native `issues` run, successful preparation, and the Goal invocation. Verify
220: that an issue without `Goal` uses the standard invocation. Preserve `Goal`
221: when adding lifecycle labels.
222: 
223: For Ralph support, create an issue with `OpenCode` and `ralph` labels and
224: confirm the workflow installs `opencode-ralph-loop`, invokes
225: `opencode run --command ralph-loop`, and preserves the same OpenCode session.
226: The build is accepted only when the session emits
227: `<promise>DONE</promise>`; a missing promise must not receive the `complete`
228: label. If both `Goal` and `ralph` are present, Ralph takes precedence.
229: 
230: For custom-branch support, set `branch` in hidden `omgithub-request:v1` metadata.
231: Verify preparation strips routing metadata, resolves the branch, and supplies
232: a frozen commit to checkout. Reject invalid or missing branches before execution.
233: Verify workflow code comes from the default branch.
234: 
235: For the `omo` issue label, verify that an otherwise normal OpenCode issue causes
236: the OpenCode startup step to install `oh-my-openagent` with Bun before starting
237: the web server and launches `opencode ... --command goal` with `ulw` in the
238: objective; an issue without the `OpenCode` label must not run that installer, and the
239: `omo` label alone must not trigger a workflow. The OMO config must use its
240: native Goal command and must not register a compatibility `ulw-loop` command.
241: 
242: The log-release step must copy and upload only non-empty `.log`/`.json` files;
243: empty service logs such as `nginx.log` can make GitHub's upload API return
244: `400 Bad Content-Length`. The OpenCode response JSON remains required and must
245: be non-empty.
246: 
247: Check scripted startup/capture before delivery. Require fresh desktop/mobile PNGs outside source. Invoke OC only for script repair and require execution plus screenshot inspection. Check the durable OmSite URL in the final comment and the diagnostic response/log files in the logs release.
248: 
249: Watch a running workflow with live per-step logs using the same internal
250: endpoints as the GitHub Actions web UI:
251: 
252: ```sh
253: python3 scripts/gh-run-watch-logs.py <run-id> \
254:   --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --internal-job-id <web-job-id> --exit-status
255: ```
256: 
257: The script authenticates with `gh auth token`. GitHub's web log endpoints are
258: unsupported and may change. Unlike `gh run view --log`, they expose the
259: currently available text while a job is running. GitHub does not expose the
260: web UI's second, internal job ID through its supported API. Read it from the
261: job page's `data-job-steps-url`, whose form is
262: `.../actions/runs/<run>/jobs/<web-job-id>/steps`.
263: 
264: In the browser console on the job page, print that URL with:
265: 
266: ```js
267: document.querySelector("check-steps").dataset.jobStepsUrl
268: ```
269: 
270: The workflow may show non-fatal Node.js deprecation or Actions cache warnings.
271: 
272: For the freshest local log, connect to the temporary SSH session posted by the
273: workflow and follow the runner's current page log:
274: 
275: ```sh
276: find /home/runner/actions-runner/cached/*/_diag/pages -type f -name '*_1.log' -print
277: tail -F /home/runner/actions-runner/cached/*/_diag/pages/*_1.log
278: ```
279: 
280: The runner writes the live Actions console output to `_diag/pages` and uploads
281: step-log chunks from `_diag/blocks`. This can be ahead of `gh run view --log`
282: while a job is still running. Avoid printing environment files, tokens, or keys.
283: 
284: Use the helper to discover the posted SSH endpoint automatically:
285: 
286: ```sh
287: bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
288: ```
289: 
290: The helper checks the AgentsWeb broker `/api/registrations` endpoint first when
291: `BROKER_API_TOKEN` is available (or when `../../sshworker/workers-dashboard/.env`
292: contains it), then falls back to the workflow issue comments.
293: 
294: ## Test the local SSH tunnel service
295: 
296: Run the raw tunnel health check from the `sshworker` checkout. Set `PYTHONPATH`
297: to the checkout because the test imports the local `lolgames_tunnel` package:
298: 
299: ```sh
300: PYTHONPATH=/Users/igor/Documents/sshworker \
301:   /Users/igor/Documents/sshworker/tests/test-ssh-tunnel.sh
302: ```
303: 
304: Interpret the output in this order:
305: 
306: - `PASS control TCP` confirms that the local machine can reach the broker
307:   control port.
308: - `PASS local SSH listener` confirms that the local SSH service is listening.
309: - `PASS registered` and `PASS SSH host-key exchange` confirm the complete
310:   public tunnel path.
311: 
312: If the test reports `No module named lolgames_tunnel`, set `PYTHONPATH` as
313: shown above. Do not treat that error as a broker outage. If the module-path
314: fix is present and registration still fails, inspect the client error output
315: and then check the broker service.
316: 
317: ## Verify generated-file exclusions
318: 
319: Check that project `.gitignore` rules exist before OpenCode starts. Check both
320: root and nested projects. Stage a nested `.agents` repository, change its HEAD,
321: and confirm that delivery removes its index entry without deleting worker files.
322: Confirm that prompts leave source changes uncommitted for workflow delivery.
323: 
324: ## Recover failed issue runs
325: 
326: Create a new issue with the same title and body after installing the fix. Attach the original execution and requested mode labels. Omit status labels.
327: Retry status updates three times. Treat exhausted status-update failures as warnings so validation and delivery can continue.
328: 
329: ## Check live progress startup
330: 
331: Run the tracker with SSH disabled. Default optional SSH variables to empty strings before starting the background process. Check that the process stays alive after launch.
332: 
333: ## Check reporting failure paths
334: 
335: Extract Cloudflare URLs only from the tunnel-ready box. Reject API URLs from error lines.
336: Wait for the progress tracker to exit before appending final results. Bound local API requests.
337: Attempt failure comments and each status-label update independently when GitHub requests fail.
338: 
339: ## Test completion recovery
340: 
341: Reproduce registration failures with an Actions installation token. Retry the same completion after registration recovers. Model draft-release tag lookups as unavailable; read the draft by its release ID. Confirm checkpoint creation, validation screenshots, and draft deployment on a live runner, not only with fixture tests.
342: 
343: ## Verify live preview priority
344: 
345: Start the main workspace with `scripts/start-project.sh` after checkpointing a completed response. Publish its `Playable preview` tunnel link once. Run capture on the shared live server. Confirm the issue iframe selects the healthy live tunnel ahead of its deployed draft, and inspect the latest workspace change there.
346: 
347: ## Check validation setup ownership
348: 
349: Keep the main build prompt equal to the user request. Run existing start.sh and capture.sh directly. Create a repair fork only after startup or capture fails. Require that fork to execute changed scripts, check readiness, and inspect desktop/mobile screenshots. Save repaired scripts with the main session export. Read new draft release IDs directly from the creation response. Retry tunnel startup at most three times and route files through the control tunnel.
350: 
351: ## Preserve validation evidence
352: 
353: Exclude `.playwright-cli` output from checkpoint trees and deployment archives. Keep capture screenshots outside source and retain them when deployment fails; remove them after successful delivery. Test healthy-server reuse, stopped-server startup, missing scripts, bounded repairs, fresh PNG output, and continuation cancellation. Treat successful capture as startup-and-capture evidence.
354: 
355: ## Separate deployment retries from repairs
356: 
357: Reuse the lifecycle checkpoint when preview preparation returns repaired=false. Save again after successful OC repair. Upload new checkpoint data to OmGithub and verify the latest pointer and conversation digest. Read legacy releases only when no managed checkpoint exists. Run legacy cleanup separately with GITHUB_REPOSITORY and TRIGGER_ISSUE_NUMBER set: bash scripts/cleanup-legacy-checkpoints.sh.
358: 
359: Retry readiness and capture at most three times with bounded backoff. Return startup exit code 75 for a running server that remains unready or an unavailable public tunnel; report an exited startup process as a script failure. Retry capture without restarting the server. Preserve each capture attempt's stdout and stderr outside source. Escalate persistent script failures to OC; surface persistent DNS/network failures directly. Execute repaired scripts and inspect screenshots.
360: 
361: Retry deployment upload using the same archive and generation for transient network failures, HTTP 408/429/500/502/503/504, and explicitly signaled rate limits. Stop on cancellation, superseded generations, and permanent errors. Deploy the server's idempotent upload handler before enabling workflow retries. Test concurrent uploads, lost responses, successful-generation replay after service recreation, capture diagnostics, readiness failures, and cancellation.
362: 
363: ## Verify project file serving
364: 
365: Run `npm ci --prefix scripts/live-files --no-audit --no-fund`, then `node --test scripts/live-files.test.mjs scripts/run-record.test.mjs scripts/opencode-reporting.test.mjs`. Verify directory listings, explicit HTML transformation, root-relative module paths, package imports, CSS processing, HMR messages, encoded folder names, readable Markdown and shell files, WASM types, and missing-file 404 responses. Confirm independent OpenCode and files URLs in run registration. Preserve the final-preview tunnel and keep dist execution outside live mode.
366: 
367: Start a new worker after publishing workflow changes. Open its files URL and click index.html. Confirm that JS requests return modules rather than OpenCode HTML and that source edits update the page over the tunnel. Run project dependencies and framework-specific compatibility checks separately; do not treat generic Vite transforms as proof of project-plugin support.
368: 
369: ## Verify progress and lean delivery
370: 
371: Check the first Actions step registers the run before checkout. Render detailed steps in dark desktop/mobile views for starting, live, disconnected, and failed states. Retry temporary Actions errors without stopping page polling.
372: 
373: Test metadata-only checkpoint reads and negative caching. Force fresh full validation on resume. Simulate three launcher calls with a healthy local app and failing public endpoint; require only one startup. Return exit 75 from transient capture fixtures and prove retries never invoke OC.
374: 
375: Test diagnostic-export reuse with matching, stale, missing, and unknown session revisions. Keep nonempty logs in GitHub Releases. Keep screenshots in OmSite and checkpoint assets limited to restore data.
376: 
377: ## Auto-start screenshot captures
378: 
379: Use the default capture helper to click one visible, enabled button named Start, Play, Start game, Play game, Start now, or Play now before taking each viewport screenshot. Allow up to three seconds for delayed controls. Skip ambiguous matches, links, forms, and obscured controls. Keep capture on the menu when no eligible control appears.

381: Set `CAPTURE_AUTO_START=false` to capture the initial screen. Set `CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR` to select a project-specific start control. Keep custom capture scripts responsible for their own interactions. Run `node --test scripts/capture-start.test.mjs`. Set `PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` and optionally `CHROME_PATH` to enable the real-browser checks; set `CAPTURE_TEST_DIR` to an existing screenshot output directory.

383: ## Regress remix preview port ownership
384: 
385: Run `node --test scripts/reclaim-preview-port.test.mjs scripts/start-project.test.mjs scripts/preview-setup.test.mjs`. Start an unmanaged project server before the controller; verify the controller stops only same-user listeners whose working directory belongs to the project, starts its own server, and serves the built output through the public hostname. Reject unrelated listeners without terminating them. Check controller process health before accepting HTTP readiness. Classify persistent HTTP 4xx host rejection as a repairable app defect; retry transport and 5xx failures separately.
386: 
387: ## Verify slow remix startup
388: 
389: Run `node --test scripts/start-project.test.mjs scripts/preview-setup.test.mjs`.
390: Allow up to 600 seconds for dependency installation and a cold production build.
391: Set `STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` to override the local readiness window.

393: Restart for a changed checkpoint, an exited process, or explicit `RESTART_APP=true`.
394: Reproduce Greywatch issue 1 with its pinned snapshot; require deployment and desktop/mobile captures after its 73-second build.
395: 
396: ## Regress oversized checkpoint publication
397: 
398: Run `node --test scripts/session-checkpoint.test.mjs`. Verify a conversation above 25 MiB uploads as gzip, restores every message and part, and deduplicates unchanged saves. Keep the full conversation within the 128 MiB limit. Download managed restore payloads to a temporary file and remove it after parsing.
399: 
400: ## Diagnose provider quota failures
401: 
402: Read the runner's `opencode-run.log` before blaming browser transport or checkpoint storage. After shutdown, read the `opencode-run.log` asset from the run's `opencode-logs-<run>` release. Inspect `type: error` events and `provider.free-limit` status 429. Use [codex-app-dev/PlayGround#10](https://github.com/codex-app-dev/PlayGround/issues/10) as the quota example; issues 6–10 stopped before generating code on the free endpoint.
403: 
404: Print a bounded, categorized reason in the failed Actions step and include that reason in the terminal OmGithub run callback before the debug hold. Keep raw provider response bodies out of status messages. Connect an account provider or select a model with available quota; avoid repeated retries against an exhausted free endpoint. Inspect the worker's own quota response rather than assuming the limit belongs to the GitHub account.
405: 
406: 
407: ## Verify sequential free-model fallback
408: 
409: Default order lives in `scripts/model-chain.json`: `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free`, Fusion (only with a Copilot Fusion token), `glm-5.3-flash-free`, `mimo-v2.6-flash-free`, then `big-pickle`. A picked model (free, paid, or Fusion) runs first, then the full default chain, deduplicated. Skip known unavailable catalog free models; retain the list when discovery fails or none are live.

411: Advance on structured quota, rate-limit, model-unavailable, or transient provider-server failures. Preserve the current session and exact request. Stop on success, cancellation, credential rejection, or unrelated execution errors. Write the terminal exit marker only after the sequence finishes. Keep the connected OpenRouter fallback after the free chain when configured. Inspect `main-model`, `model-attempts.json`, and `opencode-run.log` on the worker. Run `node --test scripts/run-with-model-fallback.test.mjs` to verify ordered fallback, early success, exhaustion, restored sessions, zero-exit error events, and exact prompt preservation.
412: 
413: 
414: ## Verify recovered provider errors and final delivery
415: 
416: Use [lasseondev/PlayGround#27](https://github.com/lasseondev/PlayGround/issues/27) as the recovered-error regression. Distinguish intermediate provider errors from the final session outcome. Query the current V2 snapshot after each model attempt. Accept success only from a fresh succeeded idle marker with its completed assistant message; reject older success, busy sessions, and interrupted turns. Record native CLI exit codes separately from effective terminal outcomes.

418: Write `main-completion.json` with the verified final message ID. Match that ID in lifecycle deployment status. Wait for that message's ready generation and its complete deployment result before labeling the issue complete or allowing cleanup. Ignore earlier ready generations and retry brief reconciliation failures. Fail on the current generation's delivery error or the bounded delivery timeout. Run the fallback, lifecycle, and wait-deployment focused tests before publishing workflow changes.

## Objective
- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish wiring gameplay, verify desktop and mobile layouts, and capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts.
- Implemented gameplay definitions, save/load, combat simulation, progression, canvas rendering, and some UI/state functions.
- Reviewed `game.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css`; confirmed gameplay/UI wiring remains unfinished.

### Active
- Complete `game.js` UI/state handlers, audio, input, armory flows, animation loop, and initialization.
- Correct HUD state classes and unify scenery/backdrop theme grouping.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts; capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Finish event handlers, audio, armory flows, animation loop, and initialization in `game.js`.
2. Fix HUD class mismatches: CSS uses `.show` for boss/combo and `.hide` for aim hint; JavaScript currently toggles `active`/`visible`.
3. Align `drawScenery()` theme selection with `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()` sector grouping.
4. Run syntax checks and test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts.
5. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot, then address any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay simulation and rendering; final UI/state wiring is missing.
- `index.html`: Screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layouts, and expected HUD state classes.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- No gameplay or screenshot test has been performed.

5. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot, then address any issues found.

- `game.js`: Gameplay simulation, rendering, and unfinished UI/state wiring.

- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layouts, and expected HUD state classes.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- Gameplay and screenshot testing have not been performed.

- Complete GUNRUSH — Mutant Mile, a lightweight standalone 2D arcade shooter for phones and tablets.
- Finish gameplay wiring, test desktop and mobile layouts, and capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Swipe-to-aim, automatic fire, escalating waves and bosses, coins, weapon unlocks, and persistent upgrades.
- Colorful 2D graphics and smooth effects, suitable for low-end Android.
- Standalone HTML/CSS/JavaScript canvas game with no game-engine or external runtime dependencies.

## Decisions
- Use synthesized audio, local persistent save data, four weapon types, themed sectors, and an armory.

## Work State
### Completed
- Responsive screens, HUD, modal and armory presentation, styling, and bundled fonts are present.
- Gameplay simulation, progression, canvas rendering, and some UI/state functions are present.
- `node --check game.js` passed previously.

### Active
- Complete remaining UI/state handlers, audio, input, armory flows, animation loop, and initialization in `game.js`.
- Align HUD state classes and scenery theme selection.
- Test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts; capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and complete the remaining game wiring in `game.js`.
2. Fix HUD class mismatches and scenery theme selection.
3. Run syntax checks and test desktop and mobile gameplay/layouts.
4. Capture and inspect a current JPEG screenshot, then address any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay simulation, rendering, and remaining UI/state wiring.
- `index.html`: Screens and DOM IDs consumed by JavaScript.
- `styles.css`: Visual design, responsive layouts, and expected HUD state classes.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture helper.
- `start.sh`: App startup script.

## Important Context
- `game.js` currently ends at line 1085 with `updateHUD()`; remaining handlers and initialization need verification.
- JavaScript uses `active`/`visible` for boss, combo, and aim hint state, while CSS expects `.show` for boss/combo and `.hide` for the aim hint.
- `drawScenery()` selects themes by `(sector - 1) % THEMES.length`; `buildBackdrop()` and `getLevel()` group sectors using `floor((sector - 1) / 2)`.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked. Gameplay and screenshot testing have not been performed.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
